prize_parts.citation: for developing targeted protein degradation by induced proximity to an E3 ubiquitin ligase, through the PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the molecular basis of glue degraders

statement.case_for: My first-round position holds after reading all eight statements. Four of us put B036 first and the other four name it as an alternative, but I weigh the science, not the count. The test I apply is whether the structure and mechanism were actually determined. Here they were: crystal structures of VHL and cereblon ternary complexes explain selectivity and cooperativity, cereblon was identified biochemically as the thalidomide target, and degradation kinetics, cooperativity and the hook effect are measured quantitatively in many independent laboratories. The result is a transferable design principle, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, and it has given chemists access to targets without a druggable pocket. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the heterobifunctional concept, and Handa identified cereblon, so the three names mark the originating discoveries for the two halves of one principle. I do not change my configuration.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so the practical impact is still partly prospective, and I would want the citation to honour the principle and its mechanism, not a pipeline. The three-name cut leaves out Ciulli, whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs non-peptidic and drug-like, as well as Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito. The citation also joins two discoveries made at different times by different groups, and Linke, Somfai and Sparr are right that a reader could see that as two achievements under one heading. I accept that cost. If the committee insists on a PROTAC-only citation, the better trio is Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, and I would vote for that over giving up B036.

responses.point: Chabes proposes centring the citation on induced proximity to an E3 ligase, with bifunctional degraders as the engineered version and thalidomide-class glues as the discovered version of the same mechanism, and accepts Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as second best.
responses.response: I adopt this framing for the citation, which answers the chair's scope question. It makes the three names defensible because each stands for a distinct element of one principle: the concept, its demonstration, and the molecular identification of cereblon. I accept his argument that cereblon is what anchors the glue half, and that Ciulli's work refines a concept already shown in cells. I still rate that refinement highly, and that is why Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli is my fallback.

responses.point: Aili answers my Ciulli challenge by saying that swapping him for Handa would drop the cereblon discovery, the only direct explanation of the thalidomide-class glues, and leans toward the wider degrader citation.
responses.response: That persuades me on the third name. Without Handa the citation covers only the engineered modality, and the mechanistic explanation of drugs already in patients would be missing. I had treated Ciulli's structural rationalisation as nearly co-equal and now rank it as a later and very important refinement. I agree with him on the wider citation. My view on perovskites is unchanged, because their stability and lead toxicity are unresolved and the credit is spread over six names.

responses.point: Linke says that after two decades there is still no approved PROTAC, that Handa's cereblon work and the PROTAC concept are two different achievements, and that B014's attribution is easier to explain.
responses.response: His point on two achievements is fair, and the induced-proximity wording is my answer to it: one mechanistic principle with two routes to it. On timing I still say the test is a reproduced and structurally explained mechanism, which B036 has. I read the in vivo condensate debate as a measurement problem and not only a matter of caution, because the evidence for a liquid phase depends on how a cellular condensate is probed. If the citation were limited to reconstituted multivalent systems, the case would be cleaner but also closer to physical chemistry than to a discovery about cells. I would not put B014 first on that basis.

responses.point: Brzezinski asks how I weigh the FSM-16 priority question for B017 and notes that a mesoporous-silica prize would follow closely after the 2025 MOF and COF prize.
responses.response: I weigh it heavily, and it is a main reason B017 stays an alternative. The Mobil work (Kresge, Beck and colleagues) gave MCM-41 with a well-characterised hexagonal mesostructure, a liquid-crystal templating mechanism and a family of M41S phases. FSM-16 (Inagaki, Kuroda) was a separate route through layered kanemite and has real priority for a mesoporous silica with uniform pores. The two are not interchangeable, but a three-name cut cannot do justice to both lines, and Stucky and Zhao's later generalisation adds more claims. Proximity to 2025 is a lesser concern for me. That is why I keep B017 below B036 and cannot call it a clean prize.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can accept a single induced-proximity citation that spans PROTACs and glues, or insists on PROTAC-only with Ciulli as third name.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader makes recognition premature for members who weight clinical consequence, since my own test is reproduced and structurally explained mechanism.
Whether my continued interest in B017 reflects field bias, given the unresolved Mobil versus FSM-16 priority and the 2025 framework-materials prize.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has changed. My field overlaps with porous materials (B017), and I am a Stockholm University colleague of the Secretary, but I have no personal or institutional connection to any credited name on the shortlist and see no ground for recusal.
